questions.text:
A processor uses a 32-bit instruction format and supports byte-addressable memory access. The ISA of the processor has 150 distinct instructions. The instructions are equally divided into two types, namely R-type and I-type, whose formats are shown below.

In the OPCODE, 1 bit is used to distinguish between I-type and R-type instructions and the remaining bits indicate the operation. The processor has 50 architectural registers, and all register fields in the instructions are of equal size.
Let X be the number of bits used to encode the UNUSED field, Y be the number of bits used to encode the OPCODE field, and Z be the number of bits used to encode the immediate value/address field. The value of X + 2Y + Z is ______
questions.solution:
Find each field size:
- 150 instructions, 75 of each type. 1 bit for type + [latex]\lceil\log_2 75\rceil=7[/latex] bits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Y = 8.
- 50 registers [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\lceil\log_2 50\rceil=6[/latex] bits per register field.
- R-type: [latex]8+X+3\times6=32\Rightarrow[/latex] X = 6.
- I-type: [latex]8+2\times6+Z=32\Rightarrow[/latex] Z = 12.

[latex]X+2Y+Z=6+16+12=34[/latex]

Answer: 34

questions.text: Let [latex] L_1 [/latex] be the language represented by the regular expression [latex] b^* a b^*\left(a b^* a b^*\right)^* [/latex] and [latex] L_2=\left\{w \in(a+b)^*|| w \mid \leq 4\right\} [/latex], where [latex] |w| [/latex] denotes the length of string [latex] w [/latex]. The number of strings in [latex] L_2 [/latex] which are also in [latex] L_1 [/latex] is ___
questions.solution:
[latex]L_1=b^*ab^*(ab^*ab^*)^*[/latex]: one a followed by pairs of a's, with any b's around [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] strings with an odd number of a's.

Count strings of length [latex]\le4[/latex] with odd number of a's:
- length 1: 1 (a)
- length 2: [latex]\binom21=2[/latex]
- length 3: [latex]\binom31+\binom33=4[/latex]
- length 4: [latex]\binom41+\binom43=8[/latex]

Total [latex]=1+2+4+8=15[/latex]

Answer: 15

questions.text: Let [latex] Z_n [/latex] be the group of integers [latex] \{0,1,2, \ldots, n-1\} [/latex] with addition modulo [latex] n [/latex] as the group operation. The number of elements in the group [latex] Z_2 \times Z_3 \times Z_4 [/latex] that are their own inverses is
questions.solution:
[latex](a,b,c)[/latex] is its own inverse iff [latex]2a\equiv0\ (\text{mod }2)[/latex], [latex]2b\equiv0\ (\text{mod }3)[/latex], [latex]2c\equiv0\ (\text{mod }4)[/latex].

- [latex]Z_2[/latex]: a = 0, 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 choices
- [latex]Z_3[/latex]: b = 0 only [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1 choice
- [latex]Z_4[/latex]: c = 0, 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 choices

Total [latex]=2\times1\times2=4[/latex]

Answer: 4

questions.text:
Consider a 32-bit system with [latex]4 \mathrm{~KB} [/latex] page size and page table entries of size 4 bytes each. Assume [latex] 1 \mathrm{~KB}=2^{10} [/latex] bytes. The OS uses a 2-level page table for memory management, with the page table containing an outer page directory and an inner page table. The OS allocates a page for the outer page directory upon process creation. The OS uses demand paging when allocating memory for the inner page table, i.e., a page of the inner page table is allocated only if it contains at least one valid page table entry.
An active process in this system accesses 2000 unique pages during its execution, and none of the pages are swapped out to disk. After it completes the page accesses, let [latex] X [/latex] denote the minimum and [latex] Y [/latex] denote the maximum number of pages across the two levels of the page table of the process.
The value of [latex] X+Y [/latex] is _____
questions.solution:
Page size [latex]2^{12}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 20-bit page number. One page holds [latex]2^{12}/4=1024[/latex] entries, so 10 bits outer + 10 bits inner; each inner page-table page covers 1024 pages.

Minimum (X): the 2000 pages are contiguous [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\lceil2000/1024\rceil=2[/latex] inner pages + 1 outer page = 3.
Maximum (Y): each page falls in a different inner table, but there are only 1024 outer entries [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1024 inner pages + 1 outer = 1025.

[latex]X+Y=3+1025=1028[/latex]

Answer: 1028

questions.text:
Consider the following augmented grammar, which is to be parsed with a SLR parser. The set of terminals is [latex] \{a, b, c, d, \#, @\} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} & S^{\prime} \rightarrow S \\ & S \rightarrow S S|A a| b A c|B c| b B a \\ & A \rightarrow d \# \\ & B \rightarrow @ \end{aligned} [/latex]
Let [latex] I_0=\operatorname{CLOSURE}\left(\left\{S^{\prime} \rightarrow \bullet S\right\}\right) [/latex]. The number of items in the set [latex] \operatorname{GOTO}\left(I_0, S\right) [/latex] is ____
questions.solution:
Items of [latex]I_0[/latex] with the dot before S: [latex]S'\rightarrow\bullet S[/latex] and [latex]S\rightarrow\bullet SS[/latex]. Moving the dot:
1. [latex]S'\rightarrow S\bullet[/latex]
2. [latex]S\rightarrow S\bullet S[/latex]

Closure of item 2 (dot before S) adds all S-productions:
3-7. [latex]S\rightarrow\bullet SS,\ S\rightarrow\bullet Aa,\ S\rightarrow\bullet bAc,\ S\rightarrow\bullet Bc,\ S\rightarrow\bullet bBa[/latex]
8. [latex]A\rightarrow\bullet d\#[/latex] (from [latex]\bullet Aa[/latex])
9. [latex]B\rightarrow\bullet @[/latex] (from [latex]\bullet Bc[/latex])

Answer: 9
